name: EasyCombIn
headline: The name that closes for Easy Comb-In.
subtitle: A sub-brand naming recommendation for Just For Men Easy Comb-In — built on Stopping Power and Closing Power across three audiences.
background: Just For Men is seeking dual placement for Easy Comb-In between the Men's Shave aisle and the Women's Hair Color aisle. The test identifies which title best positions the product — with special attention to Closing Power for the Women's HC set.
objective: Which sub-brand title gives Easy Comb-In the strongest Closing Power? Does the winner hold up across male English, male Spanish and female audiences?
hypothesis: One of the proposed sub-brand titles will have greater closing power than the current “Easy Comb-In Color” title.

methodology.format: 8 digital banners + 8 landing pages — 1 title each

charts.insight: The winners travel across languages. NO OVERALL LANGUAGE GAP — 11.51% EN vs. 9.82% ES pooled across all titles — no significant difference. And the two winning titles are language-proof: Quick Fix (16.51 / 17.76) and Precision (15.93 / 17.72). ONE TITLE DOESN'T TRAVEL — “Touch-Up” collapses in Spanish: 13.59% EN vs. 2.02% ES — the only statistically significant language gap in the test. A caution flag if this title is ever considered. DIRECTIONAL WATCH-OUT — The current title leans Spanish (11.63% ES vs. 6.12% EN, directional) — renaming should be validated in Spanish-language media first.

charts.title: Closing Power on Hotjar click heat-map landing pages — All audiences
charts.insight: Winning titles focus the click. INTENT LOOKS LIKE THIS — On the winning pages, clicks pile onto one place: Add to Cart. Quick Fix and Precision show a single hot core on the buy button and little else — visitors arrive already decided. ATTENTION ≠ INTENT — “Easy Touch-Up” is the cautionary tale: the most-explored page of the test — clicks scattered over the pack, the title, the copy — and one of the lowest closing rates. The current title shows the same diffuse pattern, echoing its below-benchmark CP. Crops show the buy section of each landing page · full-length heat maps available on request.

narrative.title: What we tested
narrative.body: Stimuli: 8 sub-brand titles, one constant claim. Eight titles, identical everything else. Same pack, same claim (“Easy no-mix application”), same media — only the sub-brand title changed. 000 · CONTROL Easy Comb-In Color · 001 Targeted Hair Color · 002 Easy Touch-Up Hair Color · 003 Touch-Up Hair Color · 004 Precision Hair Color · 005 Quick Fix Hair Color · 006 Clean-Up Hair Color · 007 No Mix Hair Color.

rounds.outcome: Hypothesis confirmed — two titles beat the control with statistical significance. Recommendation: rename to Quick Fix Hair Color — all three audiences combined, and still the only title that lifts both attention and conversion versus the current name.

learnings: Women convert far below men. CP 10.70% men vs. 3.70% women pooled — a ≈3× gap, stat. sig. — even though women pause on the banners nearly 2× more (SP 3.40% vs. 1.78%). A proxy purchase: they look, but don't commit, and no title fixed it. Next step: elevate “No Mix” as a highlighted on-pack claim to speak to the female shopper.

The best name is “Quick Fix Hair Color.” The only title significantly above the control on Stopping Power and Closing Power — CP 12.42% vs. 7.01% across all audiences, rising to 17.13% among men, where the current title closes below the IEP benchmark floor. “Precision Hair Color” is a validated alternative (CP 12.33%, stat. sig.).

Spanish and English agree on the winner. No overall language gap (11.51% EN vs. 9.82% ES, n.s.) and the winning titles are language-proof: Quick Fix 16.51 / 17.76 and Precision 15.93 / 17.72. One caution: “Touch-Up” collapses in Spanish (13.59% → 2.02%, the only stat. sig. language gap of the test).
recommendations: PRIMARY · WINNER — Rename to Quick Fix Hair Color. Highest Closing Power of the test (stat. sig. above control, 12.42% all audiences) and significantly above it on Stopping Power (2.45%). Wins with men in both languages (CP 16.51% EN · 17.76% ES) and keeps the lead in the full aggregate.

VALIDATED ALTERNATIVE — Precision Hair Color. Statistically tied with Quick Fix on Closing Power (12.33% vs. 12.42%) and equally language-proof — but its Stopping Power stays at control level (1.90%), so it converts without adding attention.

BEST FOR THE FEMALE SHOPPER — No Mix Hair Color. The strongest title with women (CP 7.61%, directional) and third overall (CP total 10.28%, directional). Rather than renaming, elevate “No Mix” as a highlighted on-pack claim to speak to the Women's HC aisle shopper.

name: Mustache & Beard
headline: The claim that wins the shelf.
subtitle: A claims-attention test for Just For Men Mustache & Beard Color - 31 claims, three audiences, one KPI: Stopping Power.
background: Just For Men is seeking dual placement for Mustache & Beard Color between the Men's Shave aisle and the Women's Hair Color aisle. A test is needed to discover which claims best position the product, to inform an update to the current on-pack claims.
objective: Which claims resonate best with the target audiences?
success_criteria: Stopping Power (this test does not measure Closing Power). No hypothesis was defined for this round — the read is exploratory across claims and audiences.

audiences.name: Men EN 30-64
audiences.details: Male, age 30–64. People who match — Interests: Hair coloring, Hair products, Just For Men, or Men's grooming products.

audiences.name: Men ES 30-64
audiences.details: Male, age 30–64, Spanish. Same interests as Men EN (Hair coloring, Hair products, Just For Men, or Men's grooming products), AND speaks Spanish.

audiences.name: Women 30-64
audiences.details: Female, age 30–64. People who match — Interests: Hair coloring, Hair products, Just For Men, or Men's grooming products. Combined addressable reach ≈ 38–44MM across the three segments.

narrative.body: Three segments, same interest criteria — split by gender and language to see whether claims travel across all three. MEN · EN: Male, age 30–64, interests Hair coloring, Hair products, Just For Men, or Men's grooming products (11.3 – 13.3 MM Meta estimated size). MEN · ES: Male, age 30–64, Spanish — same interests, AND speaks Spanish (2.3 – 2.7 MM). WOMEN: Female, age 30–64, same interests (24.3 – 28.6 MM). Combined addressable reach ≈ 38–44MM across the three segments.

narrative.body: Stimuli: 31 claims across 6 themes. Same pack, same brush — only the on-pack claim changed. Example creative: Banner 005 · “3 easy steps”. rounds.outcome: With two claims already proven across every audience and four of the strongest results specifically with men, this set gives the box both safety and strength, enough range to fill front and back without repeating a single claim.

learnings: Two themes dominate the men's top 10: Moisture & nourishment (Aloe & Coconut Oil) and Ease of application each account for 3 of the top 10.
Only two claims land in every audience's top 10: “3 easy steps” and “Natural-looking color for mustache & beard”. Everything else is audience-specific.

“Aloe & Coconut Oil” repeats in 3 of the men's top 10; the strongest is “Smooth, conditioned feel with Aloe & Coconut Oil” (1.88%); “Infused with Aloe & Coconut Oil for Softer Feeling Hair” (1.70%) and “Aloe & Coconut Oil to Help Hydrate as it Colors” (1.55%) are equally valid alternates.
All 31 claims fall within the IEP benchmark band [1.18% – 2.48%] — the read ranks relative performance, not pass/fail. Pool averages: Men (EN+ES) 1.42% · Men EN 1.46% · Men ES 1.37% · Women 1.74%.
